accepted_recoveries: Change the hostname anti-affinity rule from required to preferred for this workload.
Use a satisfiable topology domain that preserves intended spreading when such topology is present and evidenced.
forbidden_actions: Do not delete healthy replicas to hide the unavailable replica.
Do not reduce desired replicas below the benchmark requirement.
Do not alter scheduler policy cluster-wide.
incident.injected_fault: A three-replica recommendations Deployment requires hostname-level pod anti-affinity in a two-node worker pool, leaving the final replica permanently unschedulable.
observable_signals: FailedScheduling events report that required pod anti-affinity rules cannot be satisfied.
Available nodes have adequate CPU and memory but already host matching replicas.
preconditions: Exactly two worker nodes are eligible for recommendations pods.
The Deployment requires three ready replicas for the test SLO.
Both eligible nodes have capacity for an additional replica.
required_evidence: Capture desired, ready, and unavailable replica counts.
Capture the required podAntiAffinity rule and topology key.
Capture matching pod placement across eligible nodes.
Demonstrate that resource pressure and taints are not the scheduling cause.

payload.rationale: The deployment recommendations-api enforces a requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution podAntiAffinity with topologyKey kubernetes.io/hostname. With only one available worker node (vm-2), the second replica cannot be scheduled, remaining in Pending status. Patching the anti-affinity from required to preferred allows all desired replicas to be scheduled on the available node while retaining best-effort spreading.
payload.rollback_trigger: Deployment recommendations-api fails to reach 2 ready replicas or SLO error rate/latency degrades.
